Core.name: The Core
Core.environment: Bright, ordered civic, Admiralty, Fleet Academy, shipyard, research, and command environments with polished stone, etched metal, disciplined infrastructure, and mature transit instrumentation.
Core.tone: Institutional confidence under growing political and scientific strain.
Core.political: Fleet and Crown authority, technical standards, central infrastructure, and pride in the systems the Core managed to preserve after the Shattering.

Verge.name: The Verge
Verge.environment: Frontier docks, markets, farms, freeports, patched textiles, working ships, crowded civilian infrastructure, local route boards, and repair yards.
Verge.tone: Lived-in pragmatism, scarcity, trade pressure, and stubborn independence.
Verge.political: Civil government, traders, escorts, and local communities bargaining for survival after generations in which Core access could not be assumed.

Shards.name: The Shards
Shards.environment: Salvage cities, scarred decks, warrens, debris corridors, repair docks, improvised engineering, patched armor, and settlements built inside the physical wreckage of lost connection.
Shards.tone: Hard survival, factional rivalry, anger, and emerging solidarity.
Shards.political: Warlords, captains, civilians, engineers, raiders, blocs, and the Silent Triarch compete for legitimacy; no single Shard experience represents the whole region.

Lattice.name: The Lattice
Lattice.environment: Reciprocal-field corridors, echo space, survey stations, anchor infrastructure, and regions where geometry, timing, and reference frames become unreliable.
Lattice.tone: Scientific awe mixed with physically objective but incompletely explained risk.
Lattice.political: Exploration and technical necessity force cross-faction cooperation; observations may be disputed, measurements must still be tested.

Corridors.name: Inter-faction Corridors
Corridors.environment: Reciprocal-field lanes, rifts, gates, convoy routes, anchor points, shear windows, orbit, docking approaches, and transit space connecting Core, Verge, Shards, and Lattice.
Corridors.tone: Movement under threat; protection, piracy, difficult navigation, and fragile cooperation.
Corridors.political: Control of passage determines food, legitimacy, and survival. Reopening a route reconnects societies that changed while separated; it does not restore the old political order automatically.
